news.title: Yemen fighting intensifies on the Red Sea coast
news.summary: Government forces launched new attacks on Houthi positions along Yemen’s Red Sea coast, while the Houthis fired into neighbouring Saudi Arabia. The escalation follows the recent loss of Mokha and an island on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The UN says more than 82,000 people have been displaced since early September, and markets remain wary about shipping and oil risk as the conflict widens again after a quieter period since 2022.

news.title: Houthis claim 58 Saudi strikes in 24 hours
news.summary: After a heavy Houthi drone and missile wave into the kingdom — including oil sites and a southern military base — Sanaa said Riyadh answered with dozens of airstrikes in a single day. Displacement in Yemen has climbed toward roughly 86,000, with some people already fleeing onward to Djibouti. Reporting also notes unanswered Saudi confirmation of the strike tallies and renewed debate in Washington about whether to re-engage militarily.

news.title: Iranian cargo ship struck in the Strait of Hormuz
news.summary: Iranian state media reported one dead and four wounded after a cargo vessel was hit near Qeshm Island early Sunday. The incident pulled attention back to Hormuz just as Houthi pressure on the Red Sea alternative route also rose. UK maritime monitors separately reported a projectile strike and fire on a vessel in the strait, underscoring how thin commercial traffic already is through the waterway.

news.title: Oman talks on Hormuz shipping postponed
news.summary: A planned regional foreign-minister meeting in Oman on Iran–Oman ideas for managing Hormuz traffic was delayed “in the interests of consensus.” The postponement, coming the same weekend as the Qeshm strike, deepens uncertainty around diplomatic options while commercial ship traffic through the strait stays low amid the wider regional war that began in late February.

news.title: Markets stay wary as Red Sea and Hormuz flashpoints stack up
news.summary: With Bab el-Mandeb under fresh Houthi pressure and Hormuz jolted by the cargo-ship strike, oil markets and insurers remain on edge. Analysts treat the two chokepoints together: even when one corridor is partially usable, stacked risk across both raises freight costs and keeps traders pricing in disruption rather than a quick return to normal shipping patterns.

aiNews.title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei calls for an AI slowdown
aiNews.summary: Amodei argued that autonomous agent “swarms” could, within 6–12 months, run a persistent botnet across the internet and cause enormous economic damage if capability keeps racing ahead of safeguards. He called for coordinated pacing across labs while saying Anthropic would not wait for rivals. Sam Altman and Elon Musk publicly agreed that the frontier needs more time for safety to catch up after recent agent-related security incidents.

aiNews.title: Amodei: AI botnet swarm could cause hundreds of billions in damage
aiNews.summary: In a longer open letter covered by Tom’s Hardware, Amodei warned that today’s models already assist with cyber ops and other high-risk tasks, while stronger successors could shrink the expertise and manpower needed for large attacks. He framed the choice as a middle path: stopping progress entirely cedes ground to authoritarian actors, but unconstrained speed is reckless without matching guardrails.

aiNews.title: Anthropic publishes September 2026 AI misuse threat report
aiNews.summary: Anthropic’s threat-intel team detailed operations it disrupted from December 2025 through August 2026 across cyber, influence, surveillance, scams, biological and conventional weapons research, and distillation. Cases used Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus; the company says it banned accounts, tightened classifiers, and shared intelligence with partners and authorities where appropriate.

aiNews.title: Hackers abused Claude to mine secrets from 1.8M Android apps
aiNews.summary: Reporting on the same threat cycle highlights financially motivated and state-linked groups that used Claude to scan large APK corpora for secrets, steal Azure AD tokens across many tenants, and automate malware and phishing workflows. Anthropic says AI agents did nearly all the work in some campaigns, then disrupted the activity and notified victims and industry partners.

aiNews.title: Claude formalizes Fermat’s Last Theorem in 13M lines of Lean
aiNews.summary: Anthropic reported that an internal Claude run, guided by the Prove2Me tooling, produced a computer-checked formalization of Fermat’s Last Theorem in about 11 days — roughly 13 million lines of Lean. The result is framed as years of specialist work compressed into days, while still showing how labor-intensive full formalization remains even with frontier models.
